notes: Mexican-leaning (sources are mostly Mexican tweets and web text) but valid for all Spanish: the app sends 'Language: Spanish' for every es-* locale. '¿no?' and '¿verdad?' are left out of the fillers on purpose: the messy-dictation rule inserts fillers before random words, and a stray 'no' would teach the model to delete real negations. 'Este' is both a filler and a demonstrative; real ones stay in the targets. 'eh' and 'este' are listed twice so they come up more often, as in real Mexican dictation. Swear stems avoid innocent prefixes: 'pinche' is exact (not 'pinch', which starts pinchar), 'cabron' not 'cabr' (cabría), 'mamon/mamad' not 'mam' (mamá), 'verga/vergaz' not 'verg' (vergüenza). Güey/wey is slang, not a swear. The last three hard cases have misheard or missing words/accents (mande/mandé, llego/llegó, nomas/nomás, oxo = OXXO). Word lists written by the maintainers with help from an LLM; not yet reviewed by a native speaker.
